ai.description: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* reaches 26 cm in length. It is dark purplish-brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a yellow-spotted venter. It features 115–120 primary annuli and a subterminal mouth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* inhabits moist, shaded areas within subtropical broadleaf forests at mid-altitudes, typically found in damp soil near streams in Nagaland, India.
ai.behavior: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* is oviparous and exhibits maternal care. Females lay clutches of 25–40 eggs in underground burrows during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis sendenyu* is endemic to the state of Nagaland in Northeast India, where it inhabits high-elevation regions within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis sendenyu* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic pulses emitted from within its subterranean or riparian habitat.
